about: Spec values of every machine preset, each field with its source. The cost model reads effective values (bwEff, tflops, layerMs) derived from these: measured for the reference ThinkPad presets, fitted per hardware family to published llama.cpp benchmarks for the rest (data/calibration.json, tools/fit-families.mjs).
conventions: bwSpec: theoretical GB/s of the memory the weights sit in (VRAM on a card, the shared memory on unified machines).

tflopsSpec: dense (no sparsity) FP16 matrix/tensor peak. On GeForce it is the FP32-accumulate rate (half the FP16-accumulate rate); on Intel INT8 TOPS / 2; on Apple M1-M4 the FP32 rate; on CPUs a BF16 AVX-512 ceiling. null when nothing usable is published (Apple M5 and later: the per-core matrix units make the FP32 rule invalid).

Cards: ramGB, hostBw and cores describe an assumed host (desktop: Ryzen 9 9950X, 64 GB DDR5-5600, 89.6 GB/s; datacenter: one EPYC 9654 socket, 768 GB, 460.8 GB/s). The presets that existed before the catalogue (rtx4090, rtx5090, h100) keep their own host assumptions.
linkBw: 32 GB/s for PCIe 4.0 x16, 64 for 5.0 x16 (x8 links halve that).
Apple fastGB is the macOS default GPU wired limit (about 2/3 of RAM up to 36 GB, 3/4 above); iGPU fastGB depends on BIOS and driver settings.
bus: [MT/s, bits] of unified memory, so bwSpec = MT/s x bits / 8 / 1000.
priceUSD: msrp and a dated street price; 2026 street prices swing weekly during a DRAM shortage. Data only.
doubtful: DGX Spark tflopsSpec 62.5 assumes the GeForce Blackwell ratio (FP16 with FP32 accumulate = FP4 sparse / 16); 125 if GB10 accumulates FP16 at full rate. fastGB 120 is an estimate.
RTX PRO 6000 tflopsSpec 500 assumes full-rate FP32 accumulate like Ada pro cards; 250 if it behaves like GeForce.
B200 per-GPU values are 8-GPU system totals / 8; SM count from secondary sources only.
Apple M2 Pro/Max/Ultra and M3/M4 tflopsSpec are derived (cores x 256 x clock); Apple publishes none after M2.
Intel tflopsSpec = INT8 / 2 (the XMX design ratio); the A770 value depends on the clock the 315 TOPS assumed.
APU tflopsSpec (890M, 860M, 8060S, 780M) = CU x 512 x max clock; laptops rarely sustain it.
CPU tflopsSpec are derived BF16 ceilings at base or all-core clocks; llama.cpp does not reach them.
Bandwidths that depend on the build: HX 370 / 285H / 8840U (LPDDR5X vs SODIMM DDR5), EPYC 9755 (614 at DDR5-6400 vs 576 at 6000), desktops (DDR5-5600 JEDEC vs 6000+ EXPO; 4 DIMMs drop to 3600).
A100 40 GB bandwidth and A100/H200 SM counts come from the product brief / whitepaper, not fetched.

machines.name: Desktop, RTX 3060 12 GB
machines.notes: tflops = dense FP16 tensor with FP32 accumulate (GeForce runs FP32-accumulate at half the FP16-accumulate rate). bw = 192 bit x 15 Gbps / 8 = 360 GB/s (bus width from NVIDIA; 15 Gbps GDDR6 is the standard 3060 12 GB spec, not on the fetched page). tflops derived: 28 SM x 1024 FP16 flop/clk/SM x 1.777 GHz = 51.0 (FP16 acc) -> 25.5 FP32 acc; per-SM rate checked against whitepaper 3090 (82 SM, 1.695 GHz -> 142.3). units = 3584 CUDA / 128. PCIe 4.0 x16. ramGB/hostBw/cores describe an assumed host (Ryzen 9 9950X, 2x32 GB DDR5-5600: 2 ch x 64 bit x 5600 MT/s / 8 = 89.6 GB/s), not the card.
uncertain: bw data rate not on fetched page
